newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: North Asia kerosene premiums rise on new demand.
newsitem.headline: North Asia kerosene premiums rise on new demand.

text.p: Strong demand for jet/kerosene fuel from North Asia for the winter has kept premiums rising despite a sharp decline to absolute prices following the recent collapse to crude prices, industry sources said on Friday.

Increased spot purchases for January arrival jet/kerosene from Japan, South Korea and China have led to a more than 50-cent rise in premiums to Singapore spot quotes, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.

Traders said a Japanese refiner earlier this week bought a 30,000-tonne cargo for arrival in the second half of January at about $2.30 a barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f basis. The last deal was done at a $1.80-premium.
The rise in demand came on the heels of a doubling of purchases by South Korea for December-delivery cargoes over November for a total of more than 10 cargoes, traders said.
Similarly, Japanese purchases for December rose to around six cargoes compared to the four it bought in November, traders said.
South Korea has already bought about four cargoes for January arrival with Japan securing four or five cargoes.
Traders said China bought three cargoes for December arrival and is currently seeking one cargo for delivery to northern China for January.
There are about two new requirements each from South Korea and Japan currently in the market, traders said.
Jet fuel prices in Singapore fell from a near six-year traded high of $34.20 a barrel last Friday to an assessed value of $31.90 a barrel on Thursday.
The fall was line with the big losses to crude prices where January Brent on London's International Petroleum Exchange fell from Friday's close of $24.54 a barrel to end at $22.15 on Wednesday.
January Brent edged up slightly on Thursday to close up 37 cents to $22.52 a barrel.

The market's collapse was attributed to bearish stock data released by American Petroleum Institute (API) on Tuesday and the flow of Iraqi crude also on the same day ater a six-year absence, traders said.
API figures showed that crude oil stocks rose 324,000 barrels, distillates stocks climbed by over two million barrels and gasoline were up by almost six million barrels.
Traders said demand from South Korea might rise to match its 10 cargo purchases in December if the startup of a new crude distillation unit (CDU) is delayed further.
LG-Caltex Oil Corp delayed the start of a 220,000-barrel-per-day CDU by a month to late December after defects were discovered in the topper's column.
